title: Checking Inverses by Composition
short: f(g(x)) = x and g(f(x)) = x confirm an inverse pair.

blocks.html: Finding an inverse involves several algebra steps, and any one can slip. Composition gives a clean test: if two functions undo each other, then doing one after the other changes nothing.
$f$ and $g$ are inverses exactly when $f(g(x)) = x$ for every $x$ in the domain of $g$ and $g(f(x)) = x$ for every $x$ in the domain of $f$. Check both orders.

$f(g(x)) = x$ says that whatever $g$ does, $f$ undoes. $g(f(x)) = x$ says the reverse. You need both, because one order can work while the other fails. For $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = \sqrt{x}$: $f(g(x)) = (\sqrt{x})^2 = x$ for $x \ge 0$, but $g(f(x)) = \sqrt{x^2} = |x|$, which is wrong for negative $x$. So they are not inverses unless you restrict the domain.

opts.task: Find the k that makes f and g inverses.

blocks.cap: Slide $k$ until $g$ becomes the mirror image of $f$ across the gold line $m$: $y = x$. That value of $k$ makes $f(g(x)) = x$.

blocks.title: A pair that fails
steps: That is not $x$. The steps were undone in the wrong order: $f$ doubles and then adds 4, so the inverse must subtract 4 first and then halve, which gives $\frac{x - 4}{2}$.

blocks.title: Cubes and cube roots
steps: $g(f(x)) = \sqrt[3]{x^3 + 1 - 1} = \sqrt[3]{x^3} = x$, for every real $x$, negatives included.

blocks.html: Testing a single number and stopping. $f(g(0)) = 0$ can happen by luck even when the functions are not inverses. A single failure does prove they are not inverses, but to prove they are, simplify $f(g(x))$ and $g(f(x))$ with $x$ left as a letter.
